newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Electrabel merger should lead to deregulation - SGB.
newsitem.headline: Electrabel merger should lead to deregulation - SGB.

text.p: A possible merger of Belgian utility groups Electrabel NV and Tractebel SA is acceptable for their shareholder Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB), provided it also means an end to government price fixing in the sector, SGB said on Wednesday.
A spokesman for the company told Reuters that if the Belgian government wanted to merge Tractebel and Electrabel, this should mean an end to regulation in the electricity sector.
"A merger should mean the end of the official fixing of electricity prices," he said.

At present the electricity sector is highly regulated, notably via the fixing of electricity prices by the government. An end to official price fixing would be a sea change for Electrabel, which has a virtual monopoly on electricity production in Belgium.
The SGB spokesman declined to say whether deregulation was a condition for SGB's approval of a merger. "This is a condition for the liberalisation of the market in Europe," he said.
Last December, the 15 European Union member states agreed on a gradual liberalisation of the EU electricity market.
An Electrabel spokesman declined comment on SGB's deregulation comment.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
